# Running External Processes

CLI applications frequently coordinate other system binaries: executing `git` commands, spawning shell scripts, launching compilers, or piping data between subprocesses.

## Spawning Subprocesses with `std::process::Command`

The standard library `Command` builder handles subprocess execution, environment configuration, and working directory management:

```rust
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};

fn get_git_commit_hash() -> Result<String> {
    let output = Command::new("git")
        .args(["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"])
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .output()
        .context("Failed to execute git process")?;

    if !output.status.success() {
        let err = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
        bail!("git rev-parse failed: {}", err.trim());
    }

    let hash = String::from_utf8(output.stdout)?
        .trim()
        .to_string();

    Ok(hash)
}
```

## Piping Data Between Commands (Unix Pipeline Emulation)

To emulate shell pipelines (`cat file.txt | grep error | wc -l`), connect the `stdout` of child process 1 into the `stdin` of child process 2:

```rust
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use anyhow::Result;

fn count_matches_in_file(pattern: &str, filepath: &str) -> Result<String> {
    // Spawn grep process with piped stdout
    let grep_child = Command::new("grep")
        .arg(pattern)
        .arg(filepath)
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .spawn()?;

    // Pipe grep stdout into wc stdin
    let wc_child = Command::new("wc")
        .arg("-l")
        .stdin(grep_child.stdout.unwrap())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .spawn()?;

    let output = wc_child.wait_with_output()?;
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
}
```

## Security Best Practice: Never Invoke via Raw Shell

Avoid `Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg(user_input)`. Spawning subshells with unsanitized user inputs introduces command injection vulnerabilities. Always invoke executable binaries directly and pass arguments as distinct array items.
